facts.text: Best-before is about quality. Use-by is about safety.
Food can still be sold after its best-before date, but not after its use-by date.
Use-by food can be frozen before its date to keep it longer, and should be used straight after thawing.
Food past its use-by date shouldn't be eaten even if it looks and smells fine.

quiz.scenario: Chicken thigh fillets. Use by: yesterday. Looks and smells fine.
quiz.why: Use-by is a safety date. Don't eat food past it, even if it looks and smells fine.
Freezing before the use-by date keeps meat longer. Use it straight after thawing.

quiz.scenario: Sliced ham (prepacked). Use by: in 5 days.
quiz.why: Not at its date yet. Keep it in the fridge at 5°C or colder.

quiz.scenario: Dry pasta. Best before: 3 months ago.
quiz.why: Pasta is generally OK for up to a year past its best-before date.

quiz.scenario: Greek yoghurt. Best before: 5 days ago.
quiz.why: Yoghurt is generally OK for up to 2 weeks past best-before. Check it looks and smells right.

quiz.scenario: Greek yoghurt. Best before: 3 weeks ago.
quiz.why: That's outside the 2-week guidance we use, so we can't say it's OK.

quiz.scenario: Sliced bread. Best before: 6 days ago.
quiz.why: Fresh bread guidance only goes to 3 days past best-before.

quiz.scenario: Cheddar cheese. Best before: 1 month ago.
quiz.why: Hard cheese is generally OK for up to 2 months past best-before.

quiz.scenario: Long-life milk. Best before: 3 weeks ago.
quiz.why: UHT milk is generally OK for up to 8 weeks past best-before, unopened.
Not at its date yet. Store them as the label says.

quiz.scenario: Baby food pouch. Best before: 2 days ago.
quiz.why: Baby food is never shown as OK past its date.

quiz.scenario: Tin of tomatoes. Best before: next year. The tin is badly dented and swollen.
quiz.why: Damaged packaging can spoil food before its date.

firstVisit.title: Before you start
points: This app gives general guidance about date labels. It isn't medical or legal advice.
Answers assume the food is unopened, undamaged and stored as the label says.
It doesn't check allergens or ingredients.
Best-before guidance comes from Foodbank Victoria's suggestions for food relief, not a guarantee.
If in doubt, throw it out.

about.title: About this app
about.intro: Eat, Store, Freeze, Avoid helps you understand date labels. Every answer comes from one checked data file and shows where it came from. Nothing you type or photograph leaves your phone, apart from a barcode number when you scan one.
how: If the pack is damaged, swollen or leaking, or hasn't been stored as the label says: Avoid.
If there's no date on the pack: No verified info.

Use-by dates (and "Not sure") follow the use-by rules for every food: after the date, Avoid. On the date or the day before, Freeze if the food can be frozen, otherwise eat it today. Before that, Store.
If the pack has been opened: No verified info. The guidance we use covers unopened food only.
Best-before dates: on or before the date, Store. After the date, Eat if it's within the guidance window for that food, otherwise Avoid. Baby food is never shown as OK past its date.
Foods that aren't in our list get No verified info, never a guess.
gaps: How long food keeps once frozen at home
about.privacy: No accounts, cookies or tracking. Photos and camera frames are read on your phone and never uploaded. When you scan a barcode, only the barcode number is sent to Open Food Facts. Your quiz score, barcode choices and settings are kept on this phone only.

offCategories.note: Open Food Facts category tags mapped to our categories. The most specific mapped tag wins. Frozen products only match frozen categories. Every mapping needs checking, like the synonyms.

nameMustSay._note: Some products are tagged inconsistently in Open Food Facts (for example fresh milk tagged as UHT). These categories are only suggested when the product name also says one of these words; otherwise the product is treated as fresh milk, which we don't cover yet.
